scenes.tts: A patch recording gives a curve of current against tension. Can you read an area out of it?
scenes.visual: Title card: Reading a Patch. A current-tension curve with a question mark over its slope.
scenes.narration: A patch recording gives a curve of current against tension. Can you read an area out of it?

scenes.tts: Lewis and Grandl expressed mouse Pee-AY-zo one in a human cell line. They recorded cell-attached patches.
scenes.caption: Lewis and Grandl expressed mouse Piezo1 in a human cell line. They recorded cell-attached patches.
scenes.visual: A human HEK293t cell with Piezo1 channels in its membrane. A pipette approaches. Labels: mouse Piezo1, HEK293t cells.
scenes.narration: Lewis and Grandl expressed mouse Piezo1 in a human cell line. They recorded cell-attached patches.

scenes.tts: In a cell-attached patch, the pipette seals onto an intact cell. It records the channels in the membrane under its tip.
scenes.visual: Close-up: the pipette seals on the intact cell; a small dome of membrane inside the tip holds a few channels.
scenes.narration: In a cell-attached patch, the pipette seals onto an intact cell. It records the channels in the membrane under its tip.

scenes.tts: They pressurized the patch and imaged it at the same time. So the patch radius was measured, not assumed.
scenes.visual: Pressure is applied through the pipette; the patch bulges. An imaging frame measures its radius of curvature, R.
scenes.narration: They pressurized the patch and imaged it at the same time. So the patch radius was measured, not assumed.

scenes.tts: For a patch shaped like part of a sphere, pressure becomes tension. Tension equals the radius of curvature times the pressure difference, divided by two.
scenes.visual: On screen: T = R × Δp / 2. Labels: Young–Laplace relation; spherical patch, uniform tension; R = radius of curvature.
scenes.narration: For a patch shaped like part of a sphere, pressure becomes tension. Tension equals the radius of curvature times the pressure difference, divided by two.

scenes.tts: Take an illustrative patch. A radius of two micrometres, under two thousand pascals. These are invented round numbers.
scenes.visual: Illustrative values appear: R = 2.0 µm, Δp = 2000 Pa. Tag: invented round numbers.
scenes.narration: Take an illustrative patch. A radius of two micrometres, under two thousand pascals. These are invented round numbers.

scenes.tts: The tension comes out at two millinewtons per metre.
scenes.visual: Worked on screen: T = (2.0 × 10⁻⁶ m)(2000 N/m²)/2 = 2.0 × 10⁻³ N/m = 2.0 mN/m. Units cancel: m × N/m² = N/m.
scenes.narration: The tension comes out at two millinewtons per metre.

scenes.tts: Now the fit from the paper. A half-activation tension of two point seven millinewtons per metre. A slope factor of zero point eight.
scenes.visual: Fit values held on screen: T50 = 2.7 ± 0.1 mN/m, k = 0.8 ± 0.1 mN/m. The fitted curve is drawn.
scenes.narration: Now the fit from the paper. A half-activation tension of two point seven millinewtons per metre. A slope factor of zero point eight.

scenes.tts: At two millinewtons per metre, the fit predicts about twenty-nine percent of the plateau current.
scenes.visual: Worked on screen: I/Imax = 1/[1 + e^((2.7 − 2.0)/0.8)] = 1/(1 + e^0.875) ≈ 1/3.40 ≈ 0.29. A point at T = 2.0 on the curve, at 29 percent.
scenes.narration: At two millinewtons per metre, the fit predicts about twenty-nine percent of the plateau current.

scenes.tts: This fit also hides an area. You know how the slope factor relates to area. Can you find it?
scenes.visual: On screen: k = k_B·T_abs / ΔA. Find ΔA.
scenes.narration: This fit also hides an area. You know how the slope factor relates to area. Can you find it?

scenes.tts: Read it as a two-state switch, and run the fit backwards. The effective area comes out at about five square nanometres.
scenes.visual: Worked on screen: ΔA = k_B·T_abs / k = (4.1 × 10⁻²¹ J)/(0.8 × 10⁻³ N/m) = 5.1 × 10⁻¹⁸ m² ≈ 5 nm². Units cancel: J ÷ (N/m) = m². Tag: effective two-state area.
scenes.narration: Read it as a two-state switch, and run the fit backwards. The effective area comes out at about five square nanometres.

scenes.tts: Under the same reading, the effective resting preference for closed is about three point four times thermal energy. It comes from both fitted numbers, not from an independent measurement. An underestimated area alone does not tell us whether the true energy is underestimated.
scenes.visual: Worked on screen: ΔG₀,eff = T50 × ΔA_eff = (2.7 × 10⁻³ N/m)(5.1 × 10⁻¹⁸ m²) ≈ 1.4 × 10⁻²⁰ J ≈ 3.4 k_B·T_abs. Tag: effective value from both fit parameters; no general bound on the molecular energy.
scenes.narration: Under the same reading, the effective resting preference for closed is about three point four times thermal energy. It comes from both fitted numbers, not from an independent measurement. An underestimated area alone does not tell us whether the true energy is underestimated.

scenes.tts: An independent route agrees in order. Calibrated against a bacterial channel, human Pee-AY-zo one gave six to twenty square nanometres.
scenes.caption: An independent route agrees in order. Calibrated against a bacterial channel, human Piezo1 gave six to twenty square nanometres.
scenes.visual: Second estimate card: human PIEZO1 calibrated against MscL in the same patch, 6 to 20 nm² (Bae and colleagues, 2013). Placed beside the 5 nm².
scenes.narration: An independent route agrees in order. Calibrated against a bacterial channel, human Piezo1 gave six to twenty square nanometres.

scenes.tts: Both estimates assume each channel is a simple two-state switch. Hold on to that assumption.
scenes.visual: A tag pinned to both numbers: assumes a two-state switch.
scenes.narration: Both estimates assume each channel is a simple two-state switch. Hold on to that assumption.

scenes.tts: Two cautions. This is a normalized current, for mouse Pee-AY-zo one in a human cell line, at room temperature. It is not a fraction of neurons doing anything.
scenes.caption: Two cautions. This is a normalized current, for mouse Piezo1 in a human cell line, at room temperature. It is not a fraction of neurons doing anything.
scenes.visual: Caution card: normalized current; mouse Piezo1; HEK293t; room temperature; cell-attached.
scenes.narration: Two cautions. This is a normalized current, for mouse Piezo1 in a human cell line, at room temperature. It is not a fraction of neurons doing anything.

scenes.tts: And protocol matters. In a separate protocol, a five-second prepulse lowered the half-activation tension, from two point two to one point four.
scenes.visual: A second protocol panel: without prepulse T50 = 2.2 mN/m; after a 5 s +5 mmHg prepulse T50 = 1.4 mN/m.
scenes.narration: And protocol matters. In a separate protocol, a five-second prepulse lowered the half-activation tension, from two point two to one point four.

scenes.tts: The authors' reading: the prepulse relieves resting tension. Channels it had inactivated recover, so less added tension is needed.
scenes.visual: Schematic: some channels greyed as inactivated at rest; after the prepulse they recover and rejoin. Tag: authors' interpretation.
scenes.narration: The authors' reading: the prepulse relieves resting tension. Channels it had inactivated recover, so less added tension is needed.

scenes.tts: Do not mix the two protocols. The shift is the finding: the channel's sensitivity depends on the tension it was already under.
scenes.visual: A red cross over 1.4 being dropped into the 2.7 fit. Label: different protocols.
scenes.narration: Do not mix the two protocols. The shift is the finding: the channel's sensitivity depends on the tension it was already under.

scenes.tts: Read as a two-state switch, the slope factor implies an area.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: Read as a two-state switch, the slope factor implies an area. ΔA = k_B·T_abs / k. The slope factor k itself is a tension.
scenes.narration: Read as a two-state switch, the slope factor implies an area.
